test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper provides successive discounts of 7% and 2%, which are equivalent to a single discount of _______.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discount formula = a + b − (ab ÷ 100)

Given **a = 7%** and **b = 2%**.

Single discount = 7 + 2 − (7 × 2 ÷ 100)

Single discount = 9 − 0.14 = 8.86%

**∴ The correct answer is 8.86%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First discount = 7%, Second discount = 2%.
**Formulas:** Net Selling Price = MP × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)% | Equivalent Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/79829e83a90f4988ba503b176afa1984836c294cca7045a33f806fce83035193.png] 
⇒ Let **Marked Price (MP)** be 100.
⇒ After 7% discount, price = 100 − 7 = 93.
⇒ After 2% discount on 93, **Selling Price (SP)** = 93 × (98 ÷ 100) = 91.14.
⇒ Single equivalent discount = 100 − 91.14 = 8.86%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.86%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are applied one after another on the **reducing balance** of the marked price, they are called successive discounts.

Effective Discount Formula

For three successive discounts a%, b%, and c%, the single equivalent discount is found by applying the formula **a + b − ab/100** twice or using the **ratio method**.</p
